answer: Each identity registers one reef vertex, locks 70 credits, and sends a key-signed horizon sightline to every earlier vertex. The reef board publishes coordinates and obstructions for a mesh auditor to verify each horizon sightline; a missing, blocked, or wrong-key sightline forfeits the bond. The first pays 34 credits; the kth pays 34+7(k-1), so the 1000th pays 7027 and 1000 counterfeits cost 3,530,500 plus 70,000 locked bonds. A rented-vertex ring fails the key check, since its coordinates already belong to another key; an honest surveyor registers once and recovers the bond.
